meta.title: Safety and trust | {{brand.name}}
meta.description: What’s in place before, during and after every plan: how hosts prove their page is theirs, how reviews are labelled, the code of conduct, and how to report something.
meta.socialDescription: Feel good about going on your own.

sections.title: Feel good about going on your own.
sections.lead: Going to a plan on your own should feel easy. Here’s what’s in place before, during and after every plan, and what to do if something isn’t right.

rows.title: Booked on {{brand.name}}
rows.detail: The reviewer booked this plan on {{brand.name}}.

rows.title: Unverified
rows.detail: Anyone can review a page. Reviews from people who didn’t book here say so.

items.title: Before
list: Hosts prove their page is theirs before it carries their mark. Pages built from public sources say Unclaimed until then
Honest plan pages: who’s hosting, where you meet and what’s included
Reviews from people who booked are marked “Booked on {{brand.name}}”. Everyone else’s are marked Unverified

items.title: During
list: A host who is there: every plan has a host on the night
A group, not a crowd: a team, a table or a pace group, and a first hello
A quieter way to ask: with Help me say hi, you ask the host for an introduction, privately

items.title: After
list: Your name stays off public pages: they show how many are going, not who
Only your host sees the guest list for their plan
Review and report: rate the plan, and tell us privately if anything wasn’t right

sections.title: A host proves the page is theirs.
sections.lead: Some host pages start from public sources, like an Instagram account or a Luma calendar. Until the host proves the page is theirs, it says Unclaimed, and nothing on it was supplied or approved by them.

steps.title: A code from their Instagram
steps.body: The host sends us a one-time code from the page’s own Instagram account. It only works from that account, for 30 minutes.

steps.title: Or a code on their Luma calendar
steps.body: The host pastes the code into their Luma calendar’s description, and we read it on their public calendar.

steps.title: Or a review by our team
steps.body: No Instagram or Luma? The host sends links that show the page is theirs, like their website or a post that names them, and our team checks them.

card.title: What a host page can say

rows.title: Unclaimed
rows.detail: Built from public sources. The host hasn’t confirmed it yet.

rows.title: Claim under review
rows.detail: The host asked for a review, and our team is checking.

rows.title: Owner verified
rows.detail: The host proved the page is theirs.

sections.title: What everyone agrees to.
sections.lead: Everyone who uses {{brand.name}} agrees to our terms of use. These are the parts about how people treat each other, in the terms’ own words.

tiles.title: Hosts
tiles.body: Run the event as described. Honour the cancellation policy you chose. Treat every guest lawfully and respectfully.

tiles.title: Guests
tiles.body: Treat people lawfully and respectfully. No harassment, threats, stalking, discrimination or exploitation. Don’t impersonate anyone, and don’t expose anyone’s private information.

sections.title: Tell someone. We look into every report.

callout.text: In an emergency, call India’s emergency number first.

steps.title: On the night, tell your host
steps.body: They’re there to help, and can move groups or step in.

steps.title: Report it to us
steps.body: Message us on WhatsApp, or use the Help page. Only our team sees your report.

steps.title: We review it and follow up
steps.body: We look into every report and follow up with you.

items.question: Who can see that I’m going?
items.answer: Public plan pages show how many people are going, not who. Your host sees the guest list for their plan.

items.question: Are hosts checked?
items.answer: A host proves their page is theirs with a code from its Instagram account or Luma calendar, or our team checks links they send. Until then, a page built from public sources says Unclaimed.

items.question: Can I really come on my own?
items.answer: Yes. Hosts plan a group, a team or a first hello so nobody stands on their own.

items.question: How do I report something?
items.answer: Tell your host on the night, then message us on WhatsApp or use the Help page. Only our team sees your report. In an emergency, call 112.

items.question: What happens to a review I leave?
items.answer: It appears on the host’s page. If you booked the plan on {{brand.name}}, it’s marked “Booked on {{brand.name}}”; otherwise it’s marked Unverified. Hosts can reply.
